az_8_summit_crags.blurb: Summit Crags is the cluster of cliffs near the top of Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, known for long routes and wide views over the valley. Sport climbing is the largest share, followed by trad and a modest boulder field. Grades run mostly from 5.8 to 5.12, with the heart of it in the 5.10s and low 5.11s, and the boulders span V0 to V8. The Fortress and the Ravens hold most of the bolted lines, while Rappel Rock leans toward trad. At the Ravens, a row of towers climbs out of the hillside, so some shade is usually available, and many routes run 100 to 200 feet. Afternoon thunderstorms are a real concern at this height. Avalon and the Murray Wall are the other larger crags.

nh_blair_woods.blurb: Blair Woods is the biggest bouldering zone at Pawtuckaway State Park in Nottingham, where glacial erratics of granite are scattered through the forest. The problems sit within a few acres and are linked by a looping trail, so a day here means walking from block to block. The climbing is all bouldering, from V0 to V11, with a broad base of easy and middle grades and a solid group of hard problems at the top. Most visitors warm up at the Warm-up Area, then move on to the Scoop Area, Swirley Boulder or the Hero Block. The woods feel secluded and crowds are modest. Fall is the best season at Pawtuckaway, while black flies and mosquitoes are heavy in spring and early summer.

ak_valdez_area_rock.blurb: Valdez Area Rock gathers the summer cliffs around Valdez, strung along the Richardson Highway and up over Thompson Pass. The town is better known for winter ice, but the rock draws climbers once the snow clears. Sport routes make up the largest share, with some trad and a few ice lines, and grades run mostly from 5.7 to 5.11 with the biggest group around 5.10. Valdez Glacier Campground is the closest sport crag to town, a short walk through the woods, though some rock is dirty or flaky and belays can be brushy. 43 Mile is a small crag with an upper and lower wall, moderate grades and a short approach, and it is often dry when Valdez is rainy. Sunny Side and Panorama Point are also among the larger crags.

nv_eastern_nevada.blurb: Eastern Nevada is a loose collection of small climbing areas across the state's eastern ranges, with the most routes around Ely, the Toano Range and Lamoille Canyon. Sport climbing makes up well over half the routes, with a fair amount of trad, a few boulders and top-ropes, and some ice, mixed and alpine lines, including on Wheeler Peak. Grades are mostly 5.6 to 5.10, with a solid number of 5.10s and a smaller group of 5.11 to 5.13. Hercules Gap near Ely is the largest single crag: a limestone slot canyon with mostly sport routes, a busy cave sector and some bouldering nearby. The areas are far apart, so plan each stop separately.
